title: The start page of a lernapps interactive app
description: src/app.yaml of an app built from the archetype interactive (runtime @lernapps/app-templates): what the static start page says, readable without JavaScript, the app's languages and its routes, the modes or levels that each have an address app/#<id>. The build validates it against this schema, then what a schema cannot say (languages complete, restricted Markdown, unique ids), and fails with one line per problem. Every text is for learners, in plain language. A text is a string while German is the app's only language, else a map of texts by language: { de: …, en: … }.

title.description: The app's title: the h1 of the start page and of the app page, and the title of both.

description.description: What the app does and for whom, under the title of the start page.

howto.description: How to play or use the app: the keys, the goal, what counts. The start page shows it under "So geht's".

competencies.description: What a learner can do after practising with the app, each an "Ich kann …" statement. The start page lists them under "Das lernst du".

languages.description: The languages of the app, German first. Every text is then complete in each of them; each language other than German gets its own pages below /<language>/.

routes.description: Optional: the modes or levels of the app, each with its address app/#<id>, linked from the start page and listed on the app page. The core starts with the route of the address (start(seed, route)), the first one when the address names none. A topic of the app's catalog entry may link one: app/#<id>.

sections.description: Optional: background sections at the end of the start page, each a heading with its text; its id is its anchor.

id.description: A stable name, part of the address: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. Keep it once published, so that links to it keep working.

text.description: A text without formatting: a string while German is the only language of the app, else a map of texts by language ({ de: …, en: … }) with every declared language.

markdown.description: A text in restricted Markdown (paragraphs, **bold**, *italics*, lists, links, $…$ formulas; no headings, no raw HTML): a string while German is the only language of the app, else a map of texts by language.

route.description: A mode or level of the app.

title.description: Its name, the text of its links.

description.description: Optional: what it practises, next to its link on the start page.

section.description: A background section of the start page.

id.description: Its anchor on the start page: #<id>.
